Ran 11 commands, created 4 files, and 3 more tools
Eight files changed or were added, so it’s delivered as ishouldnot-update.tar.gz. Extract it at the repo root (tar -xzf ishouldnot-update.tar.gz from inside the clone) and commit. Every path in the archive is relative to the root.

Files to delete: none.

Contents:

Modified: index.html, questions.json, README.md
New: 404.html, .nojekyll, LICENSE, scripts/validate.mjs, .github/workflows/validate.yml
Your repo also has a docs/llm/vendor/claude/1.txt file, which is a saved copy of this prompt. I left it alone, but note that GitHub Pages serves it publicly.

Defects fixed in the page

64 of the “related question” links pointed to questions that didn’t exist, so most related sections were empty or missing. All now resolve.
Random and Auto-play could pick the question already on screen. Because the URL didn’t change, the page looked stuck. That can no longer happen.
All content was inserted as raw HTML. It’s now escaped, and source links only allow http and https.
og:image pointed to an image that doesn’t exist, and there was no favicon, which caused 404s on every page load. Both are fixed.
An unknown #slug used to silently show a random question. It now shows a “not found” page with suggested matches.
Smaller fixes: the page had two h1 headings, the clickable header didn’t work from the keyboard, and copying a link had no fallback. Questions also referenced image files that don’t exist.
Data corrections (the existing 35 questions were fact-checked)

Vitamin D changed from Yes to Depends. The 2024 Endocrine Society guideline and the VITAL trial don’t support routine supplements for healthy adults under 75.
Annual checkup and standing desk changed to Depends, with lower confidence.
Sleep cited the “Sleep Foundation” website but labeled it the National Sleep Foundation, which is a different organization. It now uses the AASM consensus statement and the CDC.
Double-dipping had the study backwards. Salsa is the thin dip, and it picked up the most bacteria.
Knuckle cracking described the wrong mechanism. A 2015 MRI study showed the sound comes from a bubble forming, not collapsing.
Flu misstated the 40–60% figure, which is reduction in illness, not hospitalization.
Public WiFi was outdated now that most traffic uses HTTPS.
NIST passwords now cites the 2025 final Revision 4.
Alcohol now includes the 2025 Surgeon General advisory.
About a dozen source URLs were broken by CDC, ADA, and Harvard site reorganizations, or pointed to the wrong page (for example, the medication storage source was actually the FDA disposal page).
New

56 new questions, for 91 in total, in six categories: health, food, first aid, safety, technology, and environment. Examples include car seats, smoke and CO alarms, washing raw chicken, burns, nosebleeds, MFA, ransomware, and composting.
A “Depends” verdict, plus an optional “When it’s different” section for exceptions.
Search, a Browse-all view with category and tag filters, and Previous/Next buttons.
Keyboard shortcuts, dark mode, reduced-motion support, and a medical disclaimer.
404.html, so /wear-seatbelt redirects to /#wear-seatbelt.
A CI validator that fails the build on schema errors or broken related links.
The AGPL LICENSE file. Your README claimed AGPL, but the repo didn’t include the license text.
Two things to know

I couldn’t load every source URL from here. Most are agency pages or DOIs I’m confident in. The workflow runs a non-blocking monthly link check, so check its log after the first push.
Social previews will still show the generic site title. Crawlers don’t run JavaScript or see #hash URLs, so per-question previews would need a static page for each question. That’s doable with a small generator script if you want it later.
